claim: The whole rod survives a hard two-handed push of 200 N without buckling (twice the push as margin)
law: Euler column buckling, P = pi^2 E I / L^2, pinned at both ends, 6061-T6 38.1 x 1.47 mm tube, 4.54 m: 940 N against 400 N needed. This is the ideal upper bound for a uniform tube; the slack at four couplers (0.11 mm a side) and the rod's own sag lower it (independent review)
check: 940 N ideal against 400 N needed; couplers fitted to test at TRL 4

claim: With 2 m of probe unsupported beyond the hole the tip droops by a few per cent of that length, so the tip is rested on debris beyond about 2 m
law: Cantilever d = w L^4 / 8EI + P L^3 / 3EI = 16.8 mm, plus the turn of the back span about the hole lip (pivot, grip held): 37 mm in all. The first version took the lip as a clamp (16.8 mm) and the independent review corrected it
check: 37 mm at 2 m, about 2 per cent of the length; the camera looks about 1 degree low, which the steering takes up
closed_by: VDS-CAL-001 B6b (39 mm); build plan section 5

claim: At a snap-button hole the rod keeps a safety factor of at least 2 on yield with 3 m unsupported in a void
law: Bending stress M / Z with a stress concentration of 3 at an 8.5 mm hole; 6061-T6 yield 240 MPa

claim: The two coupler pins carry a 300 N pull to free a stuck probe
law: Double shear of two 4 mm aluminium pins, tau = F / (2 n A); shear strength taken as 0.58 of 240 MPa

claim: A steering wire keeps a factor of 3 on its assumed breaking load under a 30 N thumb push against the stop
law: Lever and drum: wire tension T = F x lever / drum radius = 30 N x 50 mm / 18 mm radius (36 mm drum) = 83 N; 0.6 mm 7x7 stainless rope breaking load 250 N assumed (to confirm from the supplier)

claim: The printed PA12 hinge lugs bear the wire tension without yielding
law: Bearing stress F / (n d t) on two 2 mm pins in 2.4 mm lugs at 83 N; PA12 yield about 45 MPa (datasheet value, to confirm)

claim: The gravity drip never exceeds 5 mL/min, even with the bottle 2 m up (1 m allowed plus 1 m error) and water at 40 C
law: Hagen-Poiseuille flow in a 0.5 mm bore (5 per cent oversize as worst case), 750 mm long capillary (600 mm failed the margin, fix F3), Q = pi r^4 dP / 8 mu L (8 m of 2.5 mm tube in series lowers it further)

claim: The capillary flow is laminar, so the Poiseuille law applies
law: Reynolds number Re = rho v d / mu below 2,000 at the highest flow

claim: At the 1 m, 20 C setting the drip supplies at least half of the 2.5 L a day that Sphere gives as the survival need for drinking
law: Sphere Handbook, water supply standard 1: survival needs 2.5 to 3 litres per day (drinking and food); 88 mL/h is 2.1 L/day. The drip is a bridge until extrication, not full hydration

claim: The air path loses less than the blower can overcome at 20 L/min
law: Sum of Darcy-Weisbach pipe losses and minor losses over the filter, meter, 2.5 m hose, barbs, rod bore and outlets; blower shut-off 0.9 kPa

claim: With every outlet blocked the pressure at the tip stays below 1 kPa above ambient
law: Blower shut-off pressure is the only stop (a centrifugal blower cannot exceed its shut-off head), and it rises with the square of speed, so the blower runs from the converter's regulated output with a fixed speed cap and not straight from the pack (12.8 to 14.4 V would lift 0.9 kPa to about 1.1 to 1.3 kPa); 0.9 kPa is a datasheet figure to confirm when bought (fix F5, independent review)

claim: A 20 mm letter 1 m from the camera spans enough pixels to read
law: Pinhole geometry: 1920 pixels across a 90 degree view give 0.96 px/mm at 1 m, 19.2 px per 20 mm letter against 10 needed. This counts sensor pixels only; lens blur, compression and an analogue link can cost 30 to 50 per cent, which still leaves about 10 px (independent review)
check: 19.2 px at the sensor, about 10 px after losses
closed_by: VDS-CAL-001 C2 (19.2 px); chart test at TRL 4

claim: In moderate dust (extinction 0.5 per m, visibility about 8 m) the light after 2 m is far above the camera's minimum illumination; in dust so dense that visibility is 1 m nothing is seen, as with any camera
law: Inverse-square illuminance from 60 lm in a 120 degree beam, Beer-Lambert extinction over the 2 m round trip: 7.0 lx at 0.5 per m, 0.0064 lx at 4 per m against a 0.01 lx minimum. The first version called 0.5 per m heavy dust (independent review)
check: 7.0 lx at 0.5 per m; 0.0064 lx at 4 per m
closed_by: VDS-CAL-001 C6, C7; dust box at TRL 4

claim: After the fix (housing black anodised, emissivity 0.85; LEDs dimmed so the head dissipates 0.8 W by default) the tip housing stays at or below 48 C, the 10 minute touch limit for bare metal, at 35 C ambient
law: Same convection and radiation model; at 45 C ambient it reaches 54 C, so above 35 C ambient the tip is kept off the survivor (steered aside, as for giving water) and the LEDs are kept at the lowest useful setting; camera power at the dimmed setting is a datasheet figure to confirm when bought
closed_by: VDS-DDR-006 F1; VDS-CAL-001 K1 to K5

claim: One pack runs video and light for at least 4 h at -10 C
law: Energy balance: 76.8 Wh x 0.9 usable x 0.70 of capacity at -10 C (assumed) over an 11.1 W load (camera at full power 3 W, monitor 7 W, converter 90 %; the dimmed camera, about 0.8 W, makes the run longer)

claim: Aluminium tube with stainless pins, wire and screws and a brass air barb survives a wet shift in a collapsed building
law: Galvanic series: 6061 aluminium is anodic to stainless steel and brass, so a wet crevice corrodes the aluminium; anodising insulates, the wet time is one shift and the kit is rinsed and dried after use
check: No rate can be stated at first order; the pins and screws sit in anodised or nylon-tipped holes

claim: A LiFePO4 pack delivers its rated energy at -10 C and is charged only above 0 C
law: LiFePO4 cells discharge at low temperature with reduced capacity (70 % assumed) and must not be charged below freezing; the exact limits are on the pack datasheet, to confirm when bought
check: Charging indoors away from the kit is already a stop (build plan S2, S8)

claim: A bite valve passes water only when bitten, with 19.6 kPa of water head behind it
law: Water pressure rho g h = 19.6 kPa at 2 m; a silicone slit bite valve stays closed until bitten at a cracking pressure that must exceed it (supplier figure, not yet known)
check: Cracking pressure and the survivor's ability to bite and sip are to confirm at TRL 4 with the medical lead

claim: The assembled probe is 4.54 m long
law: Four 1,050 mm sections plus a 313 mm head plus the tail cap

claim: The setup time of 2.2 min is the sum of its steps
law: Sum of the timed steps (estimates, to time in drills)

claim: The head fits a standard 51 mm core hole
law: Geometry: largest diameter on the probe 48 mm against a 51 mm core hole, 1.5 mm a side

claim: The kit costs less than the value-engineering target
law: Sum of bom/bom.csv against budget_usd 2,000 (a control target, not a limit)

claim: Option B (after the fix): the 10 mm glass-fibre rod reaches 4 m only where the void floor or debris carries it; free reach in air is capped at 1 m
law: Cantilever droop at only 1 m is 93 mm (E 40 GPa assumed, I = 491 mm4), growing with L^3: a flexible rod cannot hold a head in free air beyond about 1 m. Fix: B is claimed only where the void floor or debris carries the rod, free reach capped at 1 m
check: Floor-supported reach plausible, to test; the first claim (4 m in free air) failed and was restated

claim: Option B: winding the rod on a 640 mm hub keeps the bending strain at about 1.5 per cent
law: Elastic strain of a rod bent on a drum, e = d / (2R + d) = 1.54 per cent, about 600 MPa at 40 GPa; that is a large share of the strength of pultruded glass-fibre rod and glass composites creep under sustained load, so a larger hub or the supplier's allowable strain is needed (independent review)
check: 1.54 per cent against an unknown allowable

claim: Option C: each tripod leg carries the 150 N hanging load with a factor of 10 against buckling
law: Euler buckling of a 32 x 2 mm aluminium tube, 1.8 m, pinned ends; load shared by three legs and taken as 150 N per leg (conservative)

claim: Option C: the sonde hangs vertical and steady on its rope and the lines hang clear in a vertical hole
law: A body hanging from an eye above its centre of mass hangs upright; it spins freely on the rope, so the picture rotates and the bite valve swings; steering is none
check: Works only down a vertical hole; side entry is not possible
